questions.question: Where was Guru Nanak Dev Ji born?
options: Rai Bhoi di Talwandi (now Nankana Sahib)
questions.explanation: Guru Nanak Dev Ji was born in 1469 at Rai Bhoi di Talwandi near Lahore, a town now known as Nankana Sahib in Pakistan.
questions.source: Britannica – Guru Nanak
questions.note: Birth month/date differs by tradition; only place asked.

questions.question: Who were the parents of Guru Nanak Dev Ji?
options: Mehta Kalu Ji and Mata Tripta Ji
Bhai Tej Bhan Ji and Mata Bakht Kaur Ji
Bhai Pheru Ji and Mata Ramo Ji
Baba Hari Das Ji and Mata Daya Kaur Ji
questions.explanation: Guru Nanak Dev Ji's father was Mehta Kalu, a village accountant, and his mother was Mata Tripta.
questions.source: Sikh Missionary Society – Guru Nanak Dev Ji

questions.question: What was the name of Guru Nanak Dev Ji's elder sister, the first to recognise his spiritual greatness?
questions.explanation: Bebe Nanaki, five years older than Guru Nanak Dev Ji, is remembered as the first person to recognise her brother's spiritual eminence.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University) – Nanaki, Bebe

questions.question: At Sultanpur Lodhi, Guru Nanak Dev Ji worked as keeper of the provision stores of which nawab?
questions.explanation: Guru Nanak Dev Ji took charge of the provision stores (modikhana) of Nawab Daulat Khan Lodi at Sultanpur Lodhi; Gurdwara Hatt Sahib marks the spot.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University) – Sultanpur Lodhi

questions.question: Who was Bebe Nanaki Ji's husband, through whose recommendation Guru Nanak Dev Ji found employment at Sultanpur Lodhi?
questions.explanation: Jai Ram, an official of Nawab Daulat Khan Lodi and husband of Bebe Nanaki, recommended his brother-in-law Guru Nanak Dev Ji for service at Sultanpur.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University) – Nanaki, Bebe

questions.question: Guru Nanak Dev Ji went into the Bein (Vein) rivulet at Sultanpur Lodhi and was not seen for some time. When did he reappear?
questions.explanation: According to the Janam Sakhis, Guru Nanak Dev Ji disappeared into the Kali Bein and re-emerged on the third day; Gurdwara Sant Ghat marks the spot where he reappeared.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University) – Sultanpur Lodhi
questions.note: Sources say 'three days' or 'two days, reappearing on the third' — phrased as 'third day' to fit both.

questions.question: What were Guru Nanak Dev Ji's first words on re-emerging from the Bein rivulet?
options: "There is no Hindu, there is no Musalman"
questions.explanation: On re-emerging, Guru Nanak Dev Ji declared, "There is no Hindu, there is no Musalman," stressing one humanity under one God.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University) – Sultanpur Lodhi

questions.question: In the Sacha Sauda ('true bargain') sakhi, what did young Nanak do with the money his father gave him for trade?
options: He fed a group of hungry sadhus
He bought cattle for the family farm
He built a dharamsal at Talwandi
He gave it to the village school
questions.explanation: Given twenty rupees to make a profitable bargain, young Nanak spent it all feeding hungry ascetics and called it the best (true) bargain he could make.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University) – Sachcha Sauda Gurdwara

questions.question: As a boy, which Hindu ceremony did Guru Nanak Dev Ji decline, asking instead for a thread of compassion, contentment and truth?
questions.explanation: When the family priest came to invest him with the janeu, young Nanak refused it, describing a spiritual thread made of compassion, contentment and truth.
questions.source: Sikhs.org – Guru Nanak

questions.question: What were the names of Guru Nanak Dev Ji's two sons?
questions.explanation: Guru Nanak Dev Ji and Mata Sulakhni had two sons, Sri Chand and Lakhmi Das. Guru Nanak Dev Ji passed over both when choosing his successor.
questions.source: Sikhs.org – Guru Nanak
questions.note: Lakhmi Das is also spelt Lakhmi Chand / Lakshmi Chand in some sources.

questions.question: Which instrument did Bhai Mardana play as Guru Nanak Dev Ji sang the Divine Word?
questions.explanation: Bhai Mardana, a Muslim bard and childhood friend, accompanied Guru Nanak Dev Ji on his travels and played the rabab while the Guru sang.
questions.source: Sikhs.org – Guru Nanak

questions.question: At Mecca, what did a qazi object to when he found Guru Nanak Dev Ji resting?
options: He was singing with a musical instrument
His feet were pointing towards the Kaaba
He was not wearing a cap
He was sitting on the qazi's prayer mat
questions.explanation: Qazi Rukn-ud-Din rebuked Guru Nanak Dev Ji for resting with his feet towards the Kaaba; the Guru asked him to turn his feet towards a direction where God's house is not.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University) – Rukn-ud-Din, Qazi

questions.question: At Haridwar, when pilgrims were throwing water east towards the sun for their ancestors, what did Guru Nanak Dev Ji do?
options: Threw water towards the west, saying he was watering his fields in Punjab
Poured the water back into a pitcher
questions.explanation: Guru Nanak Dev Ji splashed water westwards, saying he was watering his drought-hit fields; if it could not reach a few hundred miles, how could theirs reach the sun?
questions.source: Sikh Missionary Society – Guru Nanak for Children

questions.question: At Achal near Batala, Guru Nanak Dev Ji held a long discourse with which group?
options: Nath yogis (Siddhas) led by Bhangar Nath
questions.explanation: At Achal, during the Shivratri fair, Guru Nanak Dev Ji discoursed with Nath yogis led by Bhangar Nath and rejected their display of miracles in favour of the Word.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University) – Achal Sahib Gurdwara

questions.question: Which king of Sri Lanka (Ceylon) became a devotee of Guru Nanak Dev Ji according to the Janam Sakhi tradition?
questions.explanation: According to the Puratan Janam Sakhi, Raja Shivnabh of Ceylon, his queen and son became disciples, and he set up a dharamsal for congregational singing.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University) – Shivnabh, Raja
questions.note: Based on Janam Sakhi tradition; question framed accordingly.

questions.question: How many hymns of Guru Nanak Dev Ji alluding to Babar's invasions are known as Babarvani?
questions.explanation: Babarvani comprises four hymns of Guru Nanak Dev Ji — three in Raag Asa and one in Raag Tilang — describing the suffering caused by Babar's invasions.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University) – Babarvani

questions.question: Bhai Lalo, with whom Guru Nanak Dev Ji stayed at Saidpur (Eminabad) in preference to a rich official's feast, was by profession a…
questions.explanation: Bhai Lalo was a humble carpenter of Saidpur; Guru Nanak Dev Ji chose his honest bread over Malik Bhago's lavish feast.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University) – Lalo, Bhai

questions.question: Kartarpur, the town where Guru Nanak Dev Ji settled after his travels, stands on the bank of which river?
questions.explanation: Guru Nanak Dev Ji founded Kartarpur on the right bank of the Ravi (now in Pakistan) and spent his last years there.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University) – Kartarpur

questions.question: To whom did Guru Nanak Dev Ji pass on the Guruship?
questions.explanation: Bypassing his own sons, Guru Nanak Dev Ji installed his devoted disciple Bhai Lehna as his successor, naming him Angad.
questions.source: The Sikh Encyclopedia – Angad Dev, Guru

questions.question: Which bani, composed by Guru Nanak Dev Ji, appears at the very beginning of Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji?
questions.explanation: Japji Sahib, composed by Guru Nanak Dev Ji, opens Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji and is recited by Sikhs every morning.
questions.source: Sikhs.org – Guru Nanak
